display.title: Parshas Shekalim: The Half-Shekel and the Secret of Chai
display.summary_short: Every Jew gave the same half-shekel for the Mishkan's silver sockets: a lesson in unity. And the letters of 'machatzis' show that staying close to a tzaddik brings life.
display.summary_long: A talk for Shabbos Parshas Shekalim, read together with Parshas Vayakhel. Uncle Yossi explains that the half-shekel given by every man over twenty, rich and poor alike, was used, as Rashi explains, for the silver sockets that held up the tall boards of the Mishkan, where Hashem's Presence would rest. Everyone gave the same amount as a sign of achdus, and only where there is unity does the Shechinah rest, as we say in davening: 'Bless us, our Father, all of us as one.' The Alter Rebbe, in the name of the Baal Shem Tov, taught that we must love every single Jew, even one we have never met. A half-shekel shows that alone you are only half. Then a secret in the letters of machatzis: the tzaddik in the middle stands between ches and yud, which spell chai, life, while the letters furthest away, mem and sav, spell mes. Stay close to your teacher and Rebbe, who teach you Torah, and you will find true life.
display.lesson: We are complete only together with other Jews, and staying close to a tzaddik and our teachers brings true life.
